Here's a line-by-line breakdown of every change: --- ### 1. `src/controllers/anime-seasonal.js` (new file) ```js export const seasonal = (req, res) => { ``` Exports an Express route handler called `seasonal`. Takes `req` and `res` like any controller. ```js fetch(`https://api.jikan.moe/v4/seasons/now`) ``` Calls the Jikan API endpoint that returns anime airing in the current season. ```js .then((response) => response.json()) ``` Parses the Jikan response body from JSON into a JavaScript object. ```js .then((data) => res.json(data)) ``` Forwards the parsed data directly back to the client as JSON. This is the proxy pattern — our server sits between the frontend and Jikan. ```js .catch((error) => { console.dir(JSON.stringify(error)); res.status(500).json({ message: "Internal server error: " + error.message }); }); ``` If anything goes wrong (network failure, Jikan down), logs the error and sends a 500 response to the client. --- ### 2. `src/router.js` ```js import { seasonal } from "./controllers/anime-seasonal.js"; ``` Imports the new controller so it can be used as a route handler. ```js router.get("/api/anime/seasonal", seasonal); ``` Registers the route. Placed **after** `cacheMiddleware` so responses get cached (avoids hitting Jikan rate limits). Placed **before** `/api/:entityType/:id` because Express matches routes top-to-bottom — if it were after, `/api/anime/seasonal` would match `:entityType = anime`, `:id = seasonal` and hit the wrong controller. --- ### 3. `public/index.html` ```html

Seasonal Anime

Loading...

``` Adds a new section below Top Manga, following the same pattern as the existing sections. The `id="seasonal-container"` is what the JS uses to find and populate this section. The "Loading..." text shows until the fetch completes and replaces the container's content. --- ### 4. `public/app.js` ```js if (entityType === "anime" || entityType === "seasonal") { ``` The `render` function uses `entityType` to decide whether to show "eps" or "ch". Since we pass `"seasonal"` as the entityType for seasonal anime, we need this check — otherwise it would fall into the `else` branch and show "ch" (chapters) instead of "eps" (episodes). ```js const linkType = entityType === "seasonal" ? "anime" : entityType; window.location.href = `/${linkType}/${element.mal_id}`; ``` When a user clicks a card, it navigates to the detail page. Without this fix, clicking a seasonal card would go to `/seasonal/12345` which doesn't exist. This maps it to `/anime/12345` instead. ```js .then((data) => render(data, "manga")) .then(() => fetch("/api/anime/seasonal")) .then((response) => response.json()) .then((data) => render(data, "seasonal")); ``` Chains a third fetch after manga loads. Calls our new `/api/anime/seasonal` endpoint, parses the JSON, then renders it into the `seasonal-container` div. It's chained (not parallel) to avoid hammering Jikan with simultaneous requests. --- ### 5. `docs/quick-wins-todo.md` ```diff -- [ ] 5. Add seasonal anime section +- [x] 5.
